history.dynasty: Thekkumkoor (pre-Travancore); later Travancore under Marthanda Varma
history.period: Over 700 years old; ~850 AD claimed by one secondary source (UNVERIFIED)
history.summary: Renowned Vaishnava temple in Thiruvarppu village, about 8 km from Kottayam town on the Meenachil River (CSV town corrected from Kottayam). Legend: the Pandavas worshipped a four-armed Krishna idol during exile and cast it into the sea; Vilwamangalam Swamiyar (or Padmapadacharya, disciple of Adi Shankara, in variant tellings) recovered it when his boat ran aground on it, set it on a varppu (broad vessel), and the idol stuck fast - the spot became the temple, giving it the name Thiruvarppu. The murti's sankalpam is Krishna hungry after slaying Kamsa, so this is the famous 'hungry Krishna' temple: it opens daily at about 2 AM (said to be the first temple in India to open), Usha Payasam is offered at 3 AM, it stays open even during eclipses, and the priest may break the door with an axe if there is any delay. It was an important temple of the Thekkumkoor Kingdom and passed to Travancore under Marthanda Varma. Precise construction date is UNVERIFIED.

name: Thiruvarppu Sri Krishna Temple
town_description: Thiruvarppu is a village in Kottayam district about 8 km west of Kottayam town, on the banks of the Meenachil River in Kerala's midlands. It is a rural settlement known almost entirely for the Sri Krishna temple that anchors its identity. The surrounding countryside of paddy, coconut groves and the Vembanad wetlands gives it the classic Kuttanad-edge landscape of central Kerala.

travel.road: About 8 km from Kottayam town by road, on the banks of the Meenachil River

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; April-May during the annual festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Temple opens at about 2 AM daily with Usha Payasam at about 3 AM; the temple is thronged on Sundays and Thursdays (widely reported, but confirm on the ground)
